# 15. Accessibility

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Meet WCAG 2.2 AA-oriented quality for static sites through semantic HTML, perceivable content, operable UI, understandable flows, and robust code.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] An accessibility target level, normally WCAG 2.2 AA unless a stricter requirement applies.
- [ ] A semantic landmark structure for header, nav, main, footer, sections, articles, and complementary content where appropriate.
- [ ] A heading hierarchy that reflects page structure.
- [ ] Text alternatives for informative images, empty alt for decorative images, and accessible names for icon controls.
- [ ] Keyboard support for all interactive elements and visible focus indication.
- [ ] Form labels, help text, error messages, required indicators, autocomplete, and accessible validation summaries.
- [ ] Color contrast standards for text, UI components, focus indicators, and meaningful graphical objects.
- [ ] Reduced-motion support for animation, parallax, smooth scrolling, and transitions.
- [ ] Skip links or equivalent bypass mechanisms for repeated navigation on substantial pages.
- [ ] A manual assistive technology test plan for key pages and forms.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Native HTML elements must be used before custom ARIA widgets.
- [ ] ARIA must not be used to hide semantic mistakes that native markup would solve.
- [ ] All content and functionality must be available at 200 percent zoom and with text spacing adjustments where practical.
- [ ] Keyboard focus order must match visual and logical order.
- [ ] Interactive targets must be large enough and spaced enough for touch and pointer users.
- [ ] Error identification must not depend on color alone.
- [ ] Media must include captions, transcripts, or alternatives where required by content type.
- [ ] Status changes caused by JavaScript must be announced when they affect task completion.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check every template with keyboard only from top to bottom.
- [ ] Check screen reader names for navigation, buttons, links, forms, dialogs, accordions, and icons.
- [ ] Check automated accessibility reports with free tools and manually verify all critical issues.
- [ ] Check focus traps, escape behavior, scroll locking, and return focus for dialogs and menus.
- [ ] Check that links make sense out of context when possible.
- [ ] Check that images of text are avoided except unavoidable logos or screenshots with alternatives.
- [ ] Check that tables use real table markup with headers for data, and not for layout.
- [ ] Check that dynamic filtering, tabs, accordions, and validation update states correctly.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid removing outlines without an equal or better focus-visible replacement.
- [ ] Avoid div or span click handlers for controls that should be buttons or links.
- [ ] Avoid hover-only menus, keyboard traps, autoplay media, inaccessible carousels, and unlabelled icon buttons.
- [ ] Avoid placeholder text as the only label.
- [ ] Avoid color-only charts, badges, errors, required states, or active states.
- [ ] Avoid relying only on automated accessibility scores.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Accessibility must be built into markup, design, content, and QA from the beginning.
- [ ] Critical journeys must be usable without a mouse and with common screen readers.
- [ ] Accessibility defects must be treated as functional defects.
- [ ] The site must remain accessible after content updates, not only at launch.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the Python audit for common static accessibility defects such as missing alt, labels, lang, headings, button names, and focus CSS signals.
- [ ] Use optional free tools such as axe-core, Pa11y, Lighthouse, WAVE browser extension, and Playwright for deeper validation.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Accessibility strategy: usable by different abilities, without perfect vision, without a mouse, with screen readers, with keyboard, with browser zoom, with reduced motion, and without color-only meaning.
- [ ] Standards target WCAG 2.2 AA, semantic HTML, landmarks, headings, keyboard access, focus states, screen reader support, accessible links/buttons/forms/images/media, contrast, typography/readability, zoom/reflow, mobile/touch access, motion safety, navigation, skip links, components, tables/charts, cookie banner, optional controls, statement, free/open-source testing, embeds, multilingual, blog, portfolio, product, error/empty states, QA, maintenance, anti-patterns, and final approval.
- [ ] Every page has declared language, one H1, logical headings, meaningful landmarks, accessible names, form labels, useful alt text, visible focus, sufficient contrast, reduced-motion support, large touch targets, and keyboard-completable journeys.
- [ ] Do not rely on paid overlays, placeholder-only labels, hover-only interactions, color-only states, autoplay sound, inaccessible modals, tiny text, flashing effects, or trapped keyboard focus.
- [ ] Automated tools are evidence only; keyboard testing, screen reader basics, zoom, reduced motion, mobile, form errors, menus, cookie banner, and main journeys require human testing.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
